name: Analytics & Event Pipeline
tagline: Turn product events into queryable facts without slowing the product down
summary: Events are appended to a log, processed once, and stored in a columnar engine for aggregation. Everything downstream is derived and replayable, which is what makes fixing a bad transform survivable.
basis: TechFlow archetype, not a specific company's stack. It reflects the components most product-analytics and reporting pipelines share, independent of vendor.

items.note: Application emits domain events, not database rows.
Events are published only if the transaction that caused them committed.
Durable, partitioned, replayable — the backbone of the pipeline.
Partition key decides both parallelism and ordering guarantees.
Consumers lag instead of dropping data when volume spikes.
Transform and enrichment jobs; the ecosystem for data work lives here.

items.label: Stream/batch processor
items.note: Windowed aggregation now, backfills later, ideally the same logic.
Reprocessing must not double-count. Deterministic keys, upserts.
Raw events kept cheaply, so any transform can be re-run from scratch.
Columnar store for aggregate queries over billions of rows.
Curated marts and metadata that BI tools and the product read.

items.label: BI / dashboards
items.note: Analysts query the warehouse, never the production database.
Dashboard queries are repetitive; cache the expensive ones.
Consumer lag, freshness and row-count checks are the health of a pipeline.
Data freshness targets, agreed with the people who read the dashboards.

whenToUse: Product questions need aggregation over millions of events
Reporting queries are hurting the transactional database
Several teams want the same events for different purposes
You must be able to recompute history after fixing a transform
tradeoffs: Every stage adds latency: dashboards are minutes behind, not seconds
Schema changes ripple through transforms and stored aggregates
A columnar store is fast at aggregates and poor at single-row updates
Operating a streaming platform is a full engineering commitment
